key_terms.meaning: P_cr = π²EI/L_e² is the axial load at which a straight elastic column first bows sideways.
L_e = kL is the equivalent pin-ended length for a column with end conditions factor k.
λ = L_e/r compares a column's effective length with its radius of gyration.
r = √(I/A), where I is second moment of area and A is cross-section area.
1/P_R = 1/P_c + 1/P_E, often written P_R = σ_c A / (1 + aλ²), joining crushing and Euler loads.
P_c = σ_c A is the load that would squash the column material in pure compression.
e is the offset of the axial load from the column centre line.
The bending due to a small eccentricity is multiplied by sec((π/2)√(P/P_E)).
E_t is the slope of the stress-strain curve after the proportional limit; E_t < E.
σ_pl is the stress above which stress is no longer proportional to strain.
A member that carries axial compression and bending moment at the same time.
Approximately 1/(1 − P/P_E) multiplies first-order bending moments in a beam-column.
σ1 is the largest normal stress on any plane through a point.
ε1 is the largest normal strain in any direction at a point.
τ_max = (σ1 − σ3)/2 is the largest shear stress at a point.
σ_v = √(σ1² − σ1σ2 + σ2²) for plane stress; yield occurs when σ_v reaches σ_y.
A plot of stress amplitude S against cycles to failure N, usually with N on a log scale.
σ_e is the stress amplitude below which steel survives very many cycles; aluminium alloys show no true endurance limit.
σ_m = (σ_max + σ_min)/2 is the steady part of a fluctuating stress.
σ_a = (σ_max − σ_min)/2 is the half-range of a fluctuating stress.

takeaways: Euler load is a bifurcation load: a straight elastic column stays straight below it and bows above it.
Effective length turns fixed, pinned and free end conditions into an equivalent pin-ended column length.
Rankine-Gordon gives a smooth estimate for intermediate columns, between crushing load and Euler load.
Real columns have initial bow or load eccentricity, and the secant factor makes bending grow without limit at the Euler load.
Above the proportional limit the tangent modulus E_t replaces E, so inelastic buckling occurs below the Euler load.
A beam-column must be designed with amplified moments because axial compression increases bending.
Maximum principal stress and maximum principal strain theories compare a complex stress state with a simple tension test.
For ductile metals, Tresca and von Mises criteria predict yield from shear or distortion, with Tresca usually conservative.
Repeated stress below yield can cause fatigue failure; the S-N curve gives cycles to failure at a given stress amplitude.
Mean and alternating stresses combine on a constant-life diagram to give a fatigue factor of safety.
bank_note: Long answers usually stress derivation and safe use of Euler and Rankine-Gordon formulas, secant amplification for imperfect struts, beam-column moments, comparison of yield theories, and fatigue life from S-N and constant-life diagrams.

bank.q: Define the Euler buckling load for a pin-ended column and explain the meaning of every term in P_cr = π²EI/L_e².
outline: State P_cr = π²EI/L_e².
Define E, I, L_e and P_cr.
Explain that the formula assumes elastic, straight, homogeneous column.
State that the column is stable below P_cr and buckles above it.

bank.q: State the Rankine-Gordon formula and explain why it is used for intermediate columns instead of Euler load or crushing load alone.
outline: Write 1/P_R = 1/P_c + 1/P_E or equivalent.
Define P_c = σ_c A and P_E = π²EI/L_e².
Explain short-column limit tends to crushing load.
Explain long-column limit tends to Euler load.
State that intermediate columns are neither fully squash nor fully elastic buckling.

bank.q: Define maximum principal stress theory and maximum principal strain theory. For plane stress, write expressions for principal stresses from σ_x, σ_y and τ_xy.
outline: State σ1 = (σ_x + σ_y)/2 + √(((σ_x − σ_y)/2)² + τ_xy²).
State σ2 = (σ_x + σ_y)/2 − √(((σ_x − σ_y)/2)² + τ_xy²).
Maximum principal stress theory: safe if largest |σ1| or |σ2| is below yield stress.
Maximum principal strain theory: safe if largest principal strain is below yield strain in tension test.
Use ε1 = (σ1 − νσ2)/E for plane stress.

bank.q: Explain what an S-N curve shows and define endurance limit. State how aluminium alloys differ from steels in this respect.
outline: S-N curve plots stress amplitude S against cycles to failure N.
Usually N is on logarithmic scale.
Higher stress amplitude gives shorter fatigue life.
Endurance limit is stress amplitude below which steel survives very many cycles.
Aluminium alloys do not show a true endurance limit; fatigue life continues to depend on stress amplitude.

bank.q: A pin-ended aluminium strut is 2.0 m long, E = 70 GPa, I = 1.2×10⁻⁶ m⁴ and A = 600 mm². Calculate the Euler load and slenderness ratio. If yield strength is 250 MPa, decide whether Euler or Rankine-Gordon is more appropriate.
outline: Use L_e = L for pin-ended column.
Compute P_E = π²EI/L².
Compute r = √(I/A).
Compute λ = L/r.
Compare P_E/A with yield strength.
State that a very slender column is Euler-like; an intermediate column needs Rankine-Gordon.

bank.q: A column of length 3.0 m is fixed at both ends. Take k = 0.5, E = 200 GPa and I = 8.0×10⁻⁶ m⁴. Calculate the effective length and Euler buckling load.
outline: Use L_e = kL = 0.5 × 3.0 m.
Obtain L_e = 1.5 m.
Use P_cr = π²EI/L_e².
Substitute E and I in consistent units.
State final load in kN.

bank.q: A strut has a small load eccentricity e. Derive or state the secant formula and use it to find the maximum compressive stress for given P, e, A, I, E and L.
outline: Maximum stress = P/A + (P e c/I) sec((π/2)√(P/P_E)).
Define c as distance from neutral axis to extreme fibre.
Define P_E = π²EI/L².
Explain that secant factor grows as P approaches P_E.
Substitute numerical values carefully with units.

bank.q: A simply supported beam-column carries axial compression P = 0.3P_E and a transverse load giving first-order midspan moment M0 = 12 kN m. Calculate the amplified moment and maximum bending stress if the section modulus is Z = 150 cm³.
outline: Use amplification factor ≈ 1/(1 − P/P_E).
Compute factor = 1/(1 − 0.3) = 1.43 approximately.
Amplified moment = 1.43 × 12 kN m.
Bending stress = M/Z.
State that axial stress must be added separately if required.

bank.q: For plane stress, σ_x = 100 MPa, σ_y = 40 MPa and τ_xy = 30 MPa. Find principal stresses, maximum shear stress and von Mises stress. Compare with σ_yield = 250 MPa using Tresca and von Mises.
outline: Compute centre = (σ_x + σ_y)/2 = 70 MPa.
Compute radius = √(((σ_x − σ_y)/2)² + τ_xy²).
Principal stresses from centre ± radius.
τ_max = (σ1 − σ3)/2 with σ3 = 0 for plane stress.
von Mises stress for plane stress: √(σ1² − σ1σ2 + σ2²).
Check Tresca: max shear below σ_y/2; check von Mises: σ_v below σ_y.

bank.q: A component sees σ_max = 120 MPa and σ_min = 20 MPa. Find mean stress, alternating stress and stress ratio. Mark the point on a Goodman diagram and find the safety factor if σ_e = 160 MPa and σ_u = 400 MPa.
outline: Goodman line: σ_a/σ_e + σ_m/σ_u = 1 at failure.
Safety factor n from (σ_a/σ_e + σ_m/σ_u) = 1/n.

bank.q: Compare Euler, Rankine-Gordon and tangent-modulus approaches for short, intermediate and long columns. Explain which is appropriate for an aircraft strut with initial bow.
outline: Short column: yielding or crushing dominates.
Intermediate column: Rankine-Gordon or tangent-modulus approach.
Long slender column: Euler buckling dominates.
Initial bow or eccentricity makes secant amplification important.
Tangent modulus applies after proportional limit.
Aircraft strut design must consider imperfection, end fixity and material non-linearity.

bank.q: Explain why a beam-column must be designed with amplified moments. Discuss how axial compression changes stiffness and when second-order effects become large.
outline: Axial compression reduces lateral stiffness.
First-order moment M0 is multiplied by approximately 1/(1 − P/P_E).
Amplification grows rapidly as P approaches P_E.
Maximum stress combines P/A and amplified bending stress.
Second-order effects are important for slender members and high axial load.
Design must check stability, not only material strength.

bank.q: Compare Tresca, von Mises and octahedral shear criteria for ductile aircraft metals. Why do Tresca and von Mises bracket experimental yield?
outline: Tresca uses maximum shear stress = (σ1 − σ3)/2.
von Mises uses distortion energy or equivalent stress.
Octahedral shear stress is proportional to von Mises stress.
Tresca is generally conservative.
von Mises usually agrees better with ductile metal tests.
Experimental yield lies between or near these predictions depending on stress state.

bank.q: A fatigue-critical aircraft fitting has mean stress and alternating stress. Discuss how stress ratio, mean stress and surface condition affect fatigue life, and explain the use of a constant-life diagram for safety factor.
outline: Stress ratio R = σ_min/σ_max describes the cycle.
Tensile mean stress usually reduces fatigue life.
Alternating stress drives fatigue damage.
Surface finish, stress concentration and environment affect fatigue strength.
Constant-life diagram plots σ_a against σ_m for a chosen life.
Goodman or similar line gives safety factor against fatigue failure.

glossary.def: Sudden lateral deflection of a slender member under axial compression when the load reaches a critical value.
A structural member loaded mainly along its axis in compression.
The load at which a perfect column first becomes unstable in a chosen buckling mode.
The length of an equivalent pin-ended column that buckles at the same load as the real column.
The ratio L_e/r, used to classify a column as short, intermediate or long.
A section property r = √(I/A) that measures how far the area is spread from the centroid.
An empirical formula that combines crushing load and Euler load for intermediate columns.
An axial load whose line of action does not pass through the centroid of the section.
A formula for maximum stress in an eccentrically loaded column, containing sec((π/2)√(P/P_E)).
The local slope of the stress-strain curve after the proportional limit.
The highest stress for which stress remains proportional to strain.
A member carrying axial compression together with bending moment.
The increase of bending moment in a beam-column caused by axial compression acting on lateral deflection.
A normal stress on a plane where shear stress is zero.
A normal strain along a principal direction, where shear strain is zero.
A rule that predicts the stress state at which a material begins to yield.
A yield criterion based on maximum shear stress reaching the value at yield in tension.
A yield criterion based on distortion energy reaching the value at yield in tension.
Shear stress on the octahedral plane; it is proportional to the von Mises equivalent stress.
Failure by repeated or fluctuating stress at levels below the static yield strength.
A graph of stress amplitude against number of cycles to failure.
The stress amplitude below which a steel survives very many fatigue cycles.
The average of maximum and minimum stress in a fatigue cycle.
Half the difference between maximum and minimum stress in a fatigue cycle.
R = σ_min/σ_max, a measure of how a fatigue cycle is biased.
A constant-life diagram plotting alternating stress against mean stress with a straight failure line.
